correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, a selected set is total dominating exactly when it meets at least two partite classes. A nonempty complement induces one connected component exactly when it meets at least two parts or is a singleton; if it lies in one part with \(c\) vertices it has exactly \(c\) components. These two equivalences immediately give the profile criterion and every coefficient. For \(k\ge2\), the complement must be exactly \(k\) vertices of one part. When there are at least three parts, deleting an entire part still leaves selected vertices in at least two other parts; in the bipartite case it does not, which forces the strict endpoint. The published \(K_{m,n}\) formula therefore fails at \(k=n\), and the source's own \(C_4\) theorem independently exposes that conflict. The frozen exhaustive verifier matches the formulas for every multipartite profile through order ten.
correctness.risk: The classification is specific to complete multipartite graphs and a nonempty complement convention.

originality.rationale: The defining 2016 paper introduces the parameter and gives exact values for complete and complete-bipartite graphs, but not arbitrary complete multipartite graphs or an all-set enumerator. More importantly, its Proposition 3.2 includes the endpoint \(k=n\) for \(K_{m,n}\), while at that endpoint the proof's proposed selected set is an independent part and is not total dominating. The same paper's Theorem 2.6 gives \(\gamma_{tc}^2(C_4)=0\), confirming the boundary inconsistency. Fresh Resultary comparison found no later source that both repairs this endpoint and supplies the multipartite enumerator.

final_claim: For a connected complete multipartite graph, total outer-\(k\)-connected component dominating sets are characterized exactly by selected support in at least two parts and by whether the nonempty complement meets at least two parts or lies in one part. This yields the stated bivariate all-set enumerator, the exact \(k\ge2\) minima, and the strict complete-bipartite feasibility boundary \(k<\max_i n_i\), correcting the published non-strict endpoint.
limitations: Finite connected complete multipartite graphs only.
The complement is required to be nonempty under the stated convention.
